text: Understanding databases is essential for anyone working with data. There are two main types: SQL and NoSQL. SQL databases store information in tables, which are organised rows and columns, much like a spreadsheet. To get useful answers from your data, you write queries — special instructions that ask the database questions. Good data modelling helps you plan how information connects before you build anything, saving time later. Finally, indexes work like a book's contents page, helping the database find information quickly instead of searching every row. Learning these basics makes it much easier to choose the right database and use it well.
